item.title: Refactor order status strings to OrderStatus
item.brief:
Refactor the orders crate's string-based order status to a proper enum and commit the work.

Requirements:
- Add src/status.rs with pub enum OrderStatus { Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }, deriving at least Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash.
- OrderStatus::as_str(self) -> &'static str returns lowercase "pending", "paid", "shipped", "cancelled"; Display prints the same.
- Implement FromStr for OrderStatus with type Err = ParseStatusError. ParseStatusError must be public, implement std::error::Error, and its message must name the rejected input.
- Implement OrderStatus::can_transition_to(self, next: OrderStatus) -> bool: allow pending -> paid, pending -> cancelled, paid -> shipped, paid -> cancelled; reject all other transitions.
- Change Order::status to OrderStatus, re-export OrderStatus and ParseStatusError from crate root, and use the enum throughout so status string literals appear only in src/status.rs.
- Preserve observable behavior exactly, including errors, report output and ordering, and parsing.
- Run cargo test successfully and commit the changes.

Acceptance: implementation satisfies all requirements; status literals are confined to src/status.rs; cargo test passes; commit exists in the registered repository's local shipping workflow.

pr.body: Added src/status.rs for OrderStatus, ParseStatusError, lowercase parsing/display, and the allowed transition table. Updated Order, billing, shipping, and reporting to use the enum; CSV output and status count ordering are unchanged. CSV parsing preserves its prior validation order and `unknown status {:?}` error text. Added tests for parsing, transitions and rejected input. Verification: cargo fmt -- --check, cargo test (4 integration tests), and git diff --check all passed. Assumption: lowercase input remains exact and case sensitive, matching existing behavior.
pr.summary: Replaced string based order state with a typed OrderStatus enum. Callers can now use explicit states and transition rules. Before: status was stored and compared as free form strings; now: status is a four variant enum with parsing and display support.
